newsitem.title: UK: Britain offers to help Peru over guerrilla siege.
newsitem.headline: Britain offers to help Peru over guerrilla siege.

text.p: Britain on Wednesday offered Peru its help in resolving a dramatic siege of the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima and said one member of Britain's embassy staff was among the hostages.
"We stand ready to consider any request from the Peruvians for assistance," the foreign ministry said in a statement.
"We believe there is one member of the British embassy staff at the Japanese ambassador's house," it said, adding it still wished to establish whether any other Britons were inside.
Britain's ambassador to Lima, John Illman, had attended the party but left before the guerrillas began their spectacular assault late on Tuesday, the ministry said.

Some 200 high-ranking diplomats and business executives were being held hostage by about 20 heavily armed guerrillas who fired a rocket and scaled the walls of the Japanese envoy's residence amid a hail of bullets.
They are demanding the Lima government release their imprisoned comrades.
In 1980 Britain's Special Air Service (SAS) stormed the Iranian embassy in London where six guerrillas were holding 21 people hostage.
The guerrillas killed two civilians but 19 were rescued in a dramatic assault which unfurled in full view of the television cameras. Five guerrillas also died in the shoot-out.
Britain said it hoped the Peruvian authorities would be able to resolve the stand-off peacefully, but added it had stepped up security at the Japanese embassy in London as a precaution.
